clue.text: We take the responsibility on ourselves

parts.note: taken as written
ourselves, as the object of a preposition, is us

explanation.surface: A group accepts the blame for something, shouldering it collectively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We take the' is linking padding that sets the scene: the pieces are simply ON plus US, the plain word for 'ourselves'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty that falls on someone is their obligation, a synonym for responsibility.

clue.text: Something like miserly!

definitions.meaning: close to, approximately, as in 'nowhere close to the truth'
an old informal sense meaning stingy, tight-fisted

explanation.definitionFit: Close or approximate in one sense, and in a dated sense mean with money, as in 'near with his cash'.

clue.text: Shape of the hand is restricted by the foot

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: FT is the standard abbreviation for foot as a unit of length
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about how a hand's posture is limited by what the foot is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand with the fingers curled tight is one particular configuration the hand can take.

clue.text: One type of shirt or undergarment

parts.note: one, as in a lone or solitary item, is single
a T-shirt is a type of shirt, so the letter T stands for it

explanation.surface: Reads like a catalogue description of a garment that doubles as a shirt or underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a single definition, but 'One' gives SINGLE and 'type of shirt' gives T (as in T-shirt), leaving 'undergarment' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest worn under a shirt, or by athletes, is a classic piece of underwear.

clue.text: Abstaining although actually in favour of carrying the motion

parts.note: being in favour of something means being for it
bearing a load means carrying it

explanation.surface: A committee member abstains from a vote even though they actually support the motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The meeting language ('in favour of', 'motion') suggests voting, but the pieces are just FOR plus BEARING; 'the motion' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing restraint and holding back from acting or retaliating is to refrain, which is what abstaining means.

clue.text: Lack of determination of the French about where they should make a cut

indicators.note: one piece wraps around the other, as if placed about it

parts.words: where they should make a cut
parts.note: an incision is the cut a surgeon makes, the place where cutting is done
DE is French for 'of'

explanation.surface: A jibe at the French dithering over where to make spending cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to make up one's mind is irresolution, the absence of determination.

clue.text: Idiot with no feeling in his head

parts.note: something numb has lost all sensation
the skull is the bony case of the head

explanation.surface: An insult: the fool's head has no sensation in it at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-witted person is a dunce, a blockhead, which is what an idiot is.

clue.text: Bear to ring back

indicators.note: going back means reading the word for ring from right to left

parts.note: a hoop is a circular band, a ring

explanation.surface: An instruction to telephone someone back, or to put up with returning a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like a verb (to tolerate); it is the noun, the famous honey-loving teddy bear of A. A. Milne's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh is the best-known fictional teddy, so the name stands for a bear.

clue.text: Photographers harass para cooking pizza

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being mixed and worked over into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Press photographers pester a paratrooper who is making a pizza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harass' is surface padding that describes what such photographers do; 'cooking' rearranges PARA and PIZZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Freelance press snappers who pursue celebrities for candid shots are a kind of photographer.

clue.text: Plan worked out without one magistrate

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are being reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A scheme is devised that does not need a single magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tells you to remove I ('one') from MAGISTRATE before rearranging the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning scheme or ruse is a kind of plan.

clue.text: Car crashed because of electrical discharge

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters also happen to run across 'Car crashed'; that is a coincidence, the setter's device is the anagram

explanation.surface: A car crash caused by an electrical fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A luminous spark jumping across a gap between electrodes is a discharge of electricity.

clue.text: Watering holes visited by quiet, unreliable bus

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: an unreliable thing will not keep its shape, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Drinking spots that the unreliable local bus service stops at.
explanation.walkthrough: A watering hole is informal for a bar where people drink, not a pool for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars where people go to drink are jokingly called watering holes.

clue.text: Graduate, in love with a crusher!

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A university graduate has fallen for someone who crushes things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crusher' suggests a heartbreaker or a machine; it is the snake that kills by constriction.
explanation.definitionFit: A large snake that squeezes its prey to death is a constrictor, literally a crusher.

clue.text: Allowed in in pairs, but only in handcuffs

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the second

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
to let someone do something is to allow it

explanation.surface: Prisoners are admitted two at a time, but only when cuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the container signal; the second is a link. Bracelets is old slang for handcuffs, which explains the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracelets is old slang for manacles or handcuffs, worn on the wrist like jewellery.

clue.text: Chase after red dog

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: blood is red, and blood-red is a colour
to hound someone is to chase or pursue them

explanation.surface: Hunting language: pursue a red-coated hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chase after' looks like a single verb meaning pursue, but 'after' only orders the pieces and 'Chase' is a verb synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A large scent-tracking breed used to follow trails is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Sailor sent back to look for those who were missing

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word for look is turned round

parts.note: to look is to see

explanation.surface: A sailor is sent back to search for people who have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SEE into EES; it looks as if it belongs with 'sent'.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are away when expected to be present are the absent ones, those not there.

clue.text: Use of sole agent sometimes lengthens the process

indicators.note: making use of the letters means putting them to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Employing a single agent can drag out a business process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use of' signals the rearrangement; 'sometimes' and 'the process' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretching something out or making it longer is to extend it, which is what lengthening means.

clue.text: I'd be the last to bring this up!

definitions.text: I'd be the last to bring this up!

parts.words: I'd be the last to bring this up!
parts.note: the speaker is the back end of something, last in a line, and the word also means to raise or bring up a child

explanation.surface: A diplomatic speaker insists they would never mention a delicate subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as tactful reluctance; literally the hind part is 'the last', and to raise children is to bring them up.
explanation.definitionFit: The hindmost part is the back, last in position, and to raise children is to nurture them.

clue.text: Dope is very warm and taking aim at random

parts.note: dope is slang for cannabis, also called pot
is shortened to 's, as in 'it's'
very warm is hot

explanation.surface: Cannabis is very warm, and someone is firing off wild shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' contracts to S, as in 'pot's hot'. The definition is a noun idea: a random shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual, unaimed shot at a target, or a random criticism, is a wild attempt made without careful aim.

clue.text: Mizzen broken by unpopular leader giving a summons

definitions.note: describes the person who gives the call, so it stands for a noun

indicators.note: a broken mast lies in pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ship's mizzen mast is wrecked by a hated captain issuing orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpopular leader' looks like a tyrant; it is just the U that starts 'unpopular', mixed with MIZZEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who calls Muslims to prayer from a minaret is the one who summons the faithful.

clue.text: An insect on an animal can be a nuisance

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a bug is an insect
a bear is an animal

explanation.surface: An insect perched on a large animal can be very annoying to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent source of irritation or a pet hate is an annoyance, that is a nuisance.

clue.text: East's study garden

parts.note: a den is a private room, a study

explanation.surface: Someone's study looks out on a garden in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise, the biblical first home of Adam and Eve, was the original garden.

clue.text: Feeding porridge to fish can be exhausting

parts.note: gruel is a thin porridge
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Spoon-feeding porridge to fish would be a tiring job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feeding' and 'to' are surface glue: the picture of fish being fed hides a plain charade of food and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely tiring and demanding is punishing, draining, which is what exhausting means.

clue.text: Many an item is knocked down

definitions.meaning: a great quantity, as in 'a whole bunch'
at an auction an item is knocked down when sold, and each such item is so called

explanation.definitionFit: A large quantity, and an item offered for sale at auction under the hammer.

clue.text: Might be eaten or drunk

parts.note: the word names both a light afternoon or evening meal and a hot drink

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage the word also means an evening meal or afternoon snack, so it can be eaten as well as drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a hot brewed drink and, in Britain, an evening or afternoon meal.

clue.text: Start composing a poem — or a set of rules

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Begin writing verse, or else draw up some regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of laws or regulations, such as a highway or building one, is a set of rules.

clue.text: Pill works on boards

parts.note: a tablet is a pill
OPS is short for opera, Latin plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A pill acts on boards, or a pill works better taken onboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat upper surfaces of tables are flat panels, boards.

clue.text: Aims to send out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An intention to dispatch something.
explanation.definitionFit: Goals or purposes, as in 'means to an end', are aims.

clue.text: No friend can gain a stone!

parts.note: nothing or zero is O
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone without friends hopes to win a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent gemstone is a precious stone.

clue.text: Tops up to the mark

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Fill to the brim, right up to the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stain or dot is a mark.

clue.text: Can make these animals snug

indicators.note: the letters can be rearranged to make another word

explanation.surface: Some animals can be made cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest, African antelopes, are the animals meant.

clue.text: Picture monster flower

parts.note: a snap is a quick photograph, a picture
a dragon is a mythical monster

explanation.surface: A photo of a monstrous flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Antirrhinum, a garden plant with mouth-shaped blooms, is a flower.
